extracted.intended_audience: Users of GAP / computational group theorists working with character tables and class functions
extracted.subtask_description: Reference semantics and usage guidelines for GAP functions that compute, restrict/induce, manipulate, and analyze class functions and characters of finite groups (e.g., eigenvalues, determinants, tensor products, symmetrizations, Molien series, and algorithms to find irreducible characters).

rubrics_metrics.name: DeterminantOfCharacter / determinant character
rubrics_metrics.description: Compute the determinant character of a character; determinant character is well-defined for virtual characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The determinant can be computed using EigenvaluesChar (72.8.19). It is also possible to call Determinant (24.4.4) instead of DeterminantOfCharacter.

rubrics_metrics.name: EigenvaluesChar
rubrics_metrics.description: EigenvaluesChar([tbl,] chi, class) — For a character chi and an element g in the given conjugacy class of order n, return a list of length n where at position k the multiplicity of E(n)^k = exp(2πik/n) as an eigenvalue of a representation matrix affording chi is stored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Relation: chi[class] = List([1..n], k -> E(n)^k) * EigenvaluesChar(tbl, chi, class). It is also possible to call Eigenvalues (24.8.3) instead. Example usage shown for A5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tensored
rubrics_metrics.description: Tensored(chars1, chars2) — Given two lists of (values lists of) class functions of the same character table, return the list of tensor products of all entries in chars1 with all entries in chars2.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Inputs must be class functions for the same character table. Example shows Tensored on irreducible characters of A5 producing all pairwise tensor-product characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: TensorProduct (for characters)
rubrics_metrics.description: TensorProduct(chi, psi) — For characters chi and psi afforded by modules V and W, return the character afforded by the tensor product of V and W.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Equivalent to chi * psi. See also Tensored for list-of-lists tensor products. Example given for A5.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedClassFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictedClassFunction([tbl,] chi, target) — Restrict a class function chi of a group G to a subgroup H or via an injective homomorphism or character table of H; returns the restricted class function of H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If chi is a class function of a factor group F = G/N, the corresponding inflated/restricted behavior requires the factor fusion to be stored or the natural homomorphism. Syntax differs from subgroup fusion because factor fusion cannot in general be computed from groups alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: RestrictedClassFunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: RestrictedClassFunctions([tbl,] chars, target) — Like RestrictedClassFunction but takes a list chars of class functions and returns the list of restricted class functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when restricting multiple class functions at once. Examples show restricting Irr(S5) to A5 and using NaturalHomomorphismByNormalSubgroup.

rubrics_metrics.name: InducedClassFunction
rubrics_metrics.description: InducedClassFunction([tbl,] chi, H/hom/suptbl) — Induce a class function chi of a group G to a supergroup H (or via an injective homomorphism or a character table of H); returns the induced class function of H.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three allowed target forms: group H, injective homomorphism, or character table of H. See InducedClassFunctions for list variant.

rubrics_metrics.name: InducedClassFunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: InducedClassFunctions([tbl,] chars, target) — Like InducedClassFunction but takes a list chars of class functions and returns the list of induced class functions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to induce multiple class functions at once. Example shows inducing Irr(A5) to S5.

rubrics_metrics.name: InducedClassFunctionsByFusionMap
rubrics_metrics.description: InducedClassFunctionsByFusionMap(subtbl, tbl, chars, fusionmap) — Given two character tables subtbl (H) and tbl (G) and a fusion map from subtbl to tbl, return the list of induced class functions of tbl corresponding to chars with respect to the given fusion map.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This function performs the work for InducedClassFunction and InducedClassFunctions when a specific fusion map is known. Example uses PossibleClassFusions to obtain fusion maps.

rubrics_metrics.name: InducedCyclic
rubrics_metrics.description: InducedCyclic(tbl[, classes][, "all"]) — Calculate characters induced up from cyclic subgroups of the ordinary character table tbl to tbl and return the strictly sorted list of induced characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If "all" is specified, induce all irreducible characters of these subgroups; otherwise only permutation characters are calculated. If classes list is given, only cyclic subgroups generated by those classes are considered; otherwise all classes are considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReducedClassFunctions
rubrics_metrics.description: ReducedClassFunctions([tbl,][constituents,] reducibles) — Given a list reducibles of ordinary virtual characters, compute nonzero remainders and irreducibles by subtracting scalar multiples of constituents and iteratively projecting into orthogonal complements to find irreducible characters (aiming to find virtual characters of small norm, hopefully norm 1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If constituents is omitted it defaults to reducibles. Algorithm: form rems by subtracting ([reducibles[i], χ]/[χ, χ])·χ over constituents, let irrs be irreducible characters in rems, project rems into orthogonal space of irrs and repeat until no new irreducibles arise. Returns a record with components irreducibles and remainders. Example with A5 given.

rubrics_metrics.name: ReducedCharacters
rubrics_metrics.description: ReducedCharacters([tbl,] constituents, reducibles) — Similar to ReducedClassFunctions but both constituents and reducibles are assumed to be lists of characters (not general class functions); scalar products only formed when degree(constituent) ≤ degree(reducible).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use when constituents and reducibles are bona fide characters to reduce unnecessary scalar products. Algorithm and returned components analogous to ReducedClassFunctions.

rubrics_metrics.name: IrreducibleDifferences
rubrics_metrics.description: IrreducibleDifferences(tbl, reducibles, reducibles2[, scprmat]) — Return the list of irreducible characters which occur as difference of an element of reducibles and an element of reducibles2; if reducibles2 is "triangle" consider differences of elements in reducibles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Optionally provide scprmat (MatScalarProducts(tbl, reducibles, reducibles2) or MatScalarProducts(tbl, reducibles)) to avoid recomputing scalar products. Example: IrreducibleDifferences(a5, chars, "triangle") returns two A5 irreducibles.

rubrics_metrics.name: LLL (on character lattices)
rubrics_metrics.description: LLL(tbl, characters[, y][, "sort"][, "linearcomb"]) — Apply the LLL algorithm to the lattice spanned by virtual characters to find shorter vectors (virtual characters of smaller norm) and possibly irreducible characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns record with components irreducibles (found irreducible characters), remainders (list of reducible virtual characters), and norms. irreducibles together with remainders form a Z-basis of the lattice spanned by characters. Notes: remainders are not in general orthogonal to irreducibles; optional arguments: y controls sensitivity (refer to LLLReducedBasis), "sort" sorts characters and remainders by degree, "linearcomb" returns decomposition matrices irreddecomp and reddecomp expressing irreducibles/remainders in terms of input characters.

rubrics_metrics.name: Extract
rubrics_metrics.description: Extract(tbl, reducibles, grammat[, missing]) — Try to find irreducible characters by combinatorial/backtracking reasoning from scalar-product matrix grammat of reducibles; missing is optional max number of irreducibles occurring as constituents to accelerate search.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns record ext with solution (list of decomposition matrices M1..Mn) and choice (lists of indices). Interpretation: Mtr · X equals the specified sublist of reducibles; columns correspond to reducibles, rows to irreducibles. Use Decreased to examine a solution for computable irreducibles. Example demonstrates Extract + Decreased on Symmetric(4).

rubrics_metrics.name: OrthogonalEmbeddingsSpecialDimension
rubrics_metrics.description: OrthogonalEmbeddingsSpecialDimension(tbl, reducibles, grammat[, "positive"], dim) — Variant of OrthogonalEmbeddings tailored to ordinary character tables; compute orthogonal embeddings of grammat into standard lattice of dimension up to dim and then call Decreased to find irreducible characters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If vectors in reducibles are known to be proper characters, pass "positive" as fourth argument. Returns record with irreducibles (intersection of irreducibles found by Decreased across embeddings) and remainders. Example usage with S6 + LLL results shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decreased
rubrics_metrics.description: Decreased(tbl, chars, decompmat[, choice]) — Given a decomposition matrix M with M^tr · X = chars (X list of irreducible characters), try to compute the irreducibles in X or some of them; typically applied to Extract or OrthogonalEmbeddings outputs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no corresponding list X exists, Decreased returns fail; otherwise returns record with irreducibles, remainders, and matrix (decomposition matrix of remainders). For Extract input the choice component must be provided. Examples show successes and failures.

rubrics_metrics.name: DnLattice
rubrics_metrics.description: DnLattice(tbl, grammat, reducibles) — Search for sublattices isomorphic to root lattices of type D_n (n ≥ 4) in the lattice generated by reducibles; each vector in reducibles must have norm 2 and grammat is the scalar-product matrix.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DnLattice can find irreducible characters if there is a D_n lattice with n > 4; for n = 4 it may fail. Returns record with irreducibles, remainders, and gram (Gram matrix of remainders). Remainders are transformed so gram is block diagonal exhibiting lattice structure.

rubrics_metrics.name: DnLatticeIterative
rubrics_metrics.description: DnLatticeIterative(tbl, reducibles) — Iterative application of DnLattice: select norm-2 vectors, call DnLattice, reduce virtual characters with found irreducibles, repeat until no new irreducibles are found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Input reducibles may be a list of virtual characters or a record with components remainders and norms (e.g., returned by LLL). Returns record with components similar to LLL: irreducibles, norms, remainders.

rubrics_metrics.name: Symmetrizations
rubrics_metrics.description: Symmetrizations([tbl,] characters, n) — Return the list of symmetrizations of characters with the ordinary irreducible characters of the symmetric group S_n (or provide the character table of S_n instead of integer n).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition: χ[λ](g) = (1/n!) ∑_{ρ∈S_n} λ(ρ) ∏_{k=1..n} χ(g^k)^{a_k(ρ)} where a_k(ρ) is number of k-cycles of ρ. Returned list may contain zero class functions and duplicates are not deleted. Related functions: SymmetricParts, AntiSymmetricParts, OrthogonalComponents, SymplecticComponents, ExteriorPower, SymmetricPower, MinusCharacter.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricParts
rubrics_metrics.description: SymmetricParts(tbl, characters, n) — Symmetrizations of characters with the trivial character of S_n (i.e., symmetric parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience wrapper for the trivial-character symmetrization; example shows symmetric parts for A5 irreducibles at n=3.

rubrics_metrics.name: AntiSymmetricParts
rubrics_metrics.description: AntiSymmetricParts(tbl, characters, n) — Symmetrizations of characters with the sign character of S_n (i.e., antisymmetric parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Convenience wrapper for the sign-character symmetrization; examples show some results may be virtual characters (zero entries etc.).

rubrics_metrics.name: ExteriorPower (for a character)
rubrics_metrics.description: ExteriorPower(chi, n) — For a character chi afforded by module V and integer n, return the class function afforded by the n-th exterior power of V (antisymmetric power).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the symmetrization of chi with the sign character of S_n (see Symmetrizations and AntiSymmetricParts). Example lists ExteriorPower for all irreducibles of A5 with n=3.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymmetricPower (for a character)
rubrics_metrics.description: SymmetricPower(chi, n) — For character chi and integer n, return the class function afforded by the n-th symmetric power of V.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is the symmetrization of chi with the trivial character of S_n (see Symmetrizations and SymmetricParts). Example shows symmetric powers for A5 irreducibles at n=3.

rubrics_metrics.name: OrthogonalComponents (Murnaghan functions for indicator +1)
rubrics_metrics.description: OrthogonalComponents(tbl, chars, m) — For nonlinear characters with Frobenius-Schur indicator +1, return the Murnaghan components (which split χ^m into parts with generally fewer irreducible constituents) up to power m (integer between 2 and 6).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Implemented according to Murnaghan functions; if chars is a list of character objects, result entries are class function objects and there is no automatic check of the indicator, so results may contain virtual characters if indicator ≠ +1. See SymplecticComponents for indicator -1.

rubrics_metrics.name: SymplecticComponents (Murnaghan functions for indicator -1)
rubrics_metrics.description: SymplecticComponents(tbl, chars, m) — For nonlinear characters with indicator -1, return symplectic symmetrizations (Murnaghan components) of χ^m up to power m (integer between 2 and 5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Same caveat as OrthogonalComponents: no automatic checking of indicators, so results might contain virtual characters if indicators differ. Examples provided for U3(3).

rubrics_metrics.name: MolienSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: MolienSeries([tbl,] psi[, chi]) — Compute the Molien series M_{psi,chi}(z) = ∑_{d≥0} [χ, ψ[d]] z^d where ψ[d] is the symmetrization of ψ with the trivial character of S_d; default χ is the trivial character of tbl.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Returns a rational function whose MolienSeriesInfo attribute is set; denominator is represented as a product of factors (1 − z^r)^k. Use MolienSeriesInfo to get numerator/denominator decomposition and ValueMolienSeries to obtain coefficients. Example for AlternatingGroup(5) given.

rubrics_metrics.name: MolienSeriesInfo
rubrics_metrics.description: MolienSeriesInfo(ratfun) — If ratfun was constructed by MolienSeries, return a record that describes ratfun as a Molien series with components: numer, denom, ratfun, numerstring, denomstring, denominfo, summands, pol, size, degree.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides structured access to numerator/denominator and summand decomposition; special PrintObj method exists for Molien series. Example MolienSeriesInfo output shown.

rubrics_metrics.name: ValueMolienSeries
rubrics_metrics.description: ValueMolienSeries(molser, i) — Return the i-th coefficient of the Molien series computed by MolienSeries.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to extract series coefficients; example lists coefficients 0..20 for a Molien series.

rubrics_metrics.name: MolienSeriesWithGivenDenominator
rubrics_metrics.description: MolienSeriesWithGivenDenominator(molser, list) — Represent molser as a rational function with denominator ∏_{i=1}^n (1 − z^{r_i}) where list = [r1, r2, ..., rn]; return fail if such representation is not possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use to force a particular denominator factorization; example shows transformation to (1+z^15)/((1-z^10)*(1-z^6)*(1-z^2)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Possible permutation character properties
rubrics_metrics.description: When only the character table of G is available, a G-class function π that could be a permutation character (π = (1_H)^G for some H ≤ G) must satisfy a list of necessary properties (a)-(j) summarized below.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full list of properties as given: (a) π is a character of G; (b) π(g) is a nonnegative integer for all g ∈ G; (c) π(1) divides |G|; (d) π(g^n) ≥ π(g) for g ∈ G and integers n (checked only for power maps stored on the character table); (e) [π, 1_G] = 1; (f) multiplicity of any rational irreducible G-character ψ as a constituent of π is at most ψ(1)/[ψ, ψ]; (g) π(g) = 0 if order(g) does not divide |G|/π(1); (h) π(1)|N_G(g)| divides π(g)|G| for all g ∈ G; (i) π(g) ≤ (|G| − π(1))/(|g^G||Gal_G(g)|) for all nonidentity g ∈ G, where |Gal_G(g)| is number of conjugacy classes containing generators of ⟨g⟩; (j) if a prime p divides |G|/π(1) only once then s/(p−1) divides |G|/π(1) and ≡ 1 (mod p), where s is number of elements of order p in putative subgroup H (equal to number of Sylow p-subgroups in H). Any G-class function with these properties is called a possible permutation character in GAP.
